narrative: Material PL1__MAB0D63B exhibits smooth, stationary daily demand averaging 53,178 units with a low coefficient of variation of 0.18, making it well-suited to a classical (r,Q) replenishment policy. Lead times are moderately variable (CV=0.49, mean 2.46 days), driving a meaningful safety stock requirement of 107,911 units to achieve the 95% service level target. The current SAP policy carries zero safety stock and an overly conservative 4.5-day safety lead time, resulting in high ordering frequency and excess operational cost. The optimised policy consolidates orders into large EOQ-driven batches of 648,254 units, reducing total annual inventory cost by 81% from $18,907 to $3,588 while remaining well within the 1,363,206-unit storage constraint.

research_insights.selected_model: (r,Q) — Continuous-review reorder-point / fixed-order-quantity policy with EOQ
research_insights.selection_rationale: Smooth demand (CV=0.18) with no trend and moderate lead-time variability makes the classical (r,Q) EOQ model the natural fit. The policy minimises total ordering plus holding costs while the reorder point absorbs lead-time demand uncertainty via a statistically derived safety stock. No intermittency or lumpy demand patterns were detected that would require more complex models.
research_insights.boundary_risk: The storage capacity (1,363,206 units) is non-binding: safety_stock + order_quantity = 756,165 units, consuming only 55.5% of available space. No capacity-driven order reduction was required.
